newsitem.title: UK: UK October PMI index at s/a 54.5 pct, 18-month high.
newsitem.headline: UK October PMI index at s/a 54.5 pct, 18-month high.

text.p: The UK Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) rose to a seasonally adjusted 54.5 percent in October, an 18-month high, from an upwardly revised 53.5 percent in September, the Chartered Institute of Purchasing and Supply (CIPS) said.
The index showed a rise in growth in the manufacturing sector for the fifth consecutive month.

"The latest rise in output was driven by an increase in the rate of growth of new orders. This was the fifth successive monthly improvement in order books and, as in recent months, orders for consumer goods showed the greatest increase."

However, the survey also found demand spread more evenly across manufacturing in October, with stronger demand for investment goods leading to the sharpest increase in output of capital goods seen since February 1995.
The CIPS said the recent phase of growth in output prompted the first significant increase in manufacturing recruitment since March last year.
Demand for intermediate goods showed somewhat slower growth than demand for finished goods, largely reflecting stock reduction.
"The amount of goods purchased by manufacturers showed only modest growth, despite the strong growth of output, as existing stocks were used up in production," the CIPS said.

Purchasing managers have been able to run stocks at lower, more efficient, levels because both availability of inputs has been good and the prices of these purchases have been falling over the past year.

"In October, just under a fifth of all companies reported a further drop in average prices paid for materials while only around 7.0 percent saw prices rise. The prices index signalled a fall in overall prices as a result."
However, tentative signs of a tightening of price and supply conditions emerged in the October survey.

"First, the prices index, although still signalling falling prices, also registered a falling rate of decline for the third month running. Second, suppliers' delivery times showed the first lengthening in over a year."

"The increase in demand for goods from purchasing managers in recent months, although modest, was reported to have been sufficient to put pressure on some suppliers's capacity. With supply for some goods having tightened, firms have reported less success in negotiating discounts."
Following is a table of seasonally adjusted PMI indices (previously reported September figures in brackets):
OCT SEPT (pvs)
Purchasing managers' index (PMI) 54.5 53.5 (53.4)
Suppliers' delivery times 48.1 50.0 (50.1)
Quantity of purchases 52.8 54.9 (54.5)
Employment 52.6 50.5 (50.3)
Stocks of purchases 42.7 45.0 (45.2)
Stocks of finished goods 44.9 47.7 (47.6)
NOTE - The PMI is based on a weighted average of seasonally adjusted measures of output, new orders, suppliers' delivery times, stocks of items purchased and employment.

The measures are turned into indices which vary around 50 percent, a level which indicates no change on the previous month. An index reading below 50 percent indicates a decline compared with the previous month, above 50 percent indicates an increase.
-- Richard Murphy, London Newsroom 44 171 542 2774
